title: H347 stub: Attention Factor conditional latent factors for US equity statistical arbitrage
rationale: This paper achieves OOS Sharpe > 4.0 on US large-cap equities over a 24-year period using learned conditional latent factors from firm characteristic embeddings. Net of transaction costs: Sharpe 2.3. 84% improvement over SOTA statistical arbitrage. The Attention Factors are industry-sector-aligned, meaning they capture cross-sectional return relationships similar to what H343 OB filter implicitly detects. Unlike our current momentum-based approach, this paper frames the problem as joint factor learning + mispricing identification + trading policy in one end-to-end model. The GitHub code was referenced in the paper (Stanford/ACM conference) — high likelihood of reproducibility. Key relevance: (1) US large-cap universe overlaps directly with H198 30-stock universe; (2) 24-year backtest OOS period includes 2001, 2008, 2022 bear markets; (3) net-of-costs Sharpe 2.3 is comparable to our H343 OOS 3.182 but on a longer period with more regimes; (4) the attention mechanism that identifies 'weak factors explaining less variation but important for mispricing' is conceptually related to our OB filter's regime-detection property.

## H347 — Attention Factors for Statistical Arbitrage (Conditional Latent Factor Model)

**Status**: PROPOSED | **Date**: 2026-06-29 | **Source**: arXiv:2510.11616

**Paper**: Epstein, Wang, Choi, Pelger (Stanford). "Attention Factors for Statistical Arbitrage." Accepted ACM ICAIF 2025 (6th International Conference on AI in Finance).

**Hypothesis**: Replicate core Attention Factor framework on H198 30-stock large-cap universe (or expanded 100-500 stock universe). Joint learn: (1) conditional latent factors from firm characteristic cross-sections via attention mechanism; (2) mispricing signal vs factor-implied returns; (3) long-short trading policy maximizing risk-adjusted return net of costs.

**Paper Results**: OOS Sharpe > 4.0 on US large-cap equities (24-year period). Net of transaction costs: Sharpe 2.3. 84% Sharpe improvement over SOTA. Factor loadings align with industry sectors (interpretable). 'Weak factors' — those explaining less return variation — are key for identifying temporal mispricing.

**Implementation Plan**:
1. Obtain firm characteristic data (yfinance + FRED for macro features, or FMP for fundamentals)
2. Implement attention-based factor model (PyTorch, ~3-4 hidden factor layers)
3. Backtest on H198 30-stock universe first, then expand to S&P 500 if feasible
4. IS: 2000-2015, OOS: 2016-2026 (24-year full period requires pre-2008 data)
5. Gate: OOS Sharpe > 2.0 net of costs, MaxDD < 15%

**Dependencies**: PyTorch, factor characteristic data (size, value, momentum, quality). Pre-2013 data needed for 24-year period — extend H198 universe backward or use ETF proxies for regime coverage.

**Caution**: Deep learning models on 30 stocks = very high overfitting risk. Recommend regularized version (dropout + L2) and rolling-window cross-validation (H344b approach) before trusting results.

**Script**: backtesting/daily/run_h347.py (to be written)
